## Sheet: Profile
Profile
Company | Del Taco
Industry | Quick Service Restaurant (QSR) / Mexican-American Fast Food
HQ | Lake Forest, CA (25521 Commercentre Drive, Suite 200, Lake Forest, CA 92630)
Locations | ~580-600 restaurants across 15-18 states
Revenue | ~$541 Million Annually (company estimates vary $500M-$5B depending on source/scope)
Franchise? | Mixed model - approximately half company-owned/operated, half franchised. Del Taco was acquired by Yadav Enterprises from Jack in the Box in December 2025 (~$115-119 million deal); Yadav was a longtime Del Taco franchisee prior to acquisition.
Employees | ~5,100-7,300 (estimates vary by source)
Partner/Comparable Brands | Competes with Taco Bell, Chipotle, Wendy's, El Pollo Loco, Jack in the Box (former parent); part of Yadav Enterprises' broader restaurant portfolio
Articles + Relevant Intel
Growth Initiative | https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/del-taco-introduces-turnaround-plan-fresh-off-its-acquisition | Project Sunrise: Launched March 2026 under new owner Yadav Enterprises - an 18-month turnaround roadmap focused on restoring core menu consistency and quality, bold menu innovation, expanded catering, and a stronger loyalty program. Brings back the Classic Burrito line, original prep methods, and the Jack'd Up menu. Plans ~7 new locations in 2026 (incl. South Carolina), plus announced expansion into Indiana (10 units) and Kentucky (5 units).
New Leadership | https://www.qsrmagazine.com/story/under-new-ownership-del-taco-rolls-out-recovery-plan-focused-on-menu-innovation-and-loyalty/ | Noah Chillingworth returned/promoted to Chief Marketing Officer; Ellen Sasada rejoined as VP of Supply Chain, Food Safety & Quality Assurance; Ulyses Camacho (also President & COO of Taco Cabana) named Chief Transformation Officer - all part of Yadav Enterprises' post-acquisition leadership build-out.
Ownership Change | https://www.restaurantbusinessonline.com/marketing/del-tacos-turnaround-plan-brings-back-some-its-old-ways | Del Taco sold by Jack in the Box to Yadav Enterprises in Dec. 2025 for ~$115-119M (down from the ~$585M Jack in the Box paid in 2022), following multiple quarters of declining same-store sales and franchisee bankruptcies, including closures across Georgia locations.
